name: Optimize Rusty Duke ISMCTS playing strength

description: Baseline benchmark for ISMCTS strength_score

asi.hypothesis: Establish deterministic baseline across seeded 4p and h2h workloads before changing engine behavior.

description: Evaluate against average living opponent score instead of fixed half of opponent sum

asi.hypothesis: In 4-player games, dividing total opponent material by 2 over-penalizes root material; comparing root to average living opponent should improve multi-player search utility.
asi.learning: Large aggregate gain mostly from 4p random (+16 wins) and h2h (+5), but 4p heuristic dropped (-5), suggesting averaging favors survival/material enough to crush random but may need targeted aggression against heuristic opponents.

description: Add coup-pressure bonus for players with 7+ and 10+ coins in eval material score

asi.hypothesis: Coins at coup thresholds are more valuable than linear material; making eval aware of forced/imminent coups should guide rollouts/search toward timely attacks and threat avoidance.
asi.learning: Aggregate improves to 99 with better 4p heuristic and h2h, while 4p random loses some of the previous gain. Decisions drop sharply, indicating games resolve faster with coup-pressure-aware choices.

description: Increase hidden influence material weight from 10 to 12

asi.hypothesis: Survival/influence may be underweighted relative to coins after adding coup-pressure; a larger hidden-card weight might improve long-horizon choices.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 88, mostly hurting both 4-player workloads despite fewer timeouts.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep hidden influence at 10; if tuning eval, vary coin/coup pressure or attack targeting rather than raw influence weight.

description: Decrease hidden influence material weight from 10 to 8

asi.hypothesis: More aggressive coin/action valuation by lowering influence weight might convert more games into wins.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 87, mainly collapsing 4p_random wins; reduced influence weight over-aggresses or undervalues survival.
asi.next_action_hint: Leave influence weight at 10; tune move heuristics or selection rather than broad material scaling.

description: Increase coup-pressure eval bonuses from 5/8 to 7/12

asi.hypothesis: Stronger bonus for having enough coins to coup could improve urgency around coup threats after the initial 5/8 bonus helped.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 97; 4p heuristic did not improve and 4p random stayed below the 5/8 version.
asi.next_action_hint: Current 7+=5 and 10+=8 coup-pressure bonuses are close to better; test smaller/lower values or asymmetric opponent threat penalties if continuing eval tuning.

description: Decrease coup-pressure eval bonuses from 5/8 to 3/5

asi.hypothesis: A milder coup-threshold bonus might keep the previous h2h/heuristic benefits without overcommitting to coup pressure.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 97; 4p random improved but 4p heuristic dropped to 14/60.
asi.next_action_hint: Coup pressure creates tradeoffs between random and heuristic opponents; consider opponent-specific threat terms or rollout heuristic scoring rather than simple global bonus size.

description: Raise heuristic rollout Coup base score from 80 to 100

asi.hypothesis: Heuristic rollouts may under-prioritize guaranteed coups; raising Coup score could make search rollouts resolve threats more decisively.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 98; h2h dropped by 2 wins while 4p gains were insufficient.
asi.next_action_hint: Coup is already prioritized enough by base 80 plus eval coup-pressure; avoid increasing direct Coup heuristic globally.

description: Lower heuristic rollout Coup base score from 80 to 70

asi.hypothesis: The eval coup-pressure bonus may make direct Coup heuristic over-prioritized; lowering base Coup might improve setup play and h2h.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 98 despite h2h improving to 47; both 4-player workloads worsened.
asi.next_action_hint: Coup base 80 balances multiplayer better; h2h-specific improvement suggests future multi-objective tuning may need separate benchmark weighting.

description: Choose final ISMCTS move by visit count instead of mean reward

asi.hypothesis: Robust-child selection by visit count may be less noisy than mean-reward final choice at only 60 iterations.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 98; 4p random improved but 4p heuristic and h2h worsened.
asi.next_action_hint: Mean reward final selection is better for this low-iteration benchmark; if revisiting, try hybrid visit threshold or lower-confidence penalized mean.

description: Remove random jitter from heuristic rollout move scoring

asi.hypothesis: Heuristic rollout noise may degrade search estimates; deterministic scoring could make rollouts more consistent.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 92. H2h improved strongly, but both 4-player workloads collapsed; jitter appears important for diverse multi-player rollouts and avoiding legal-order bias.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep small jitter. If tuning, vary jitter magnitude or tie-breaking only; don't remove stochasticity entirely.

description: Increase heuristic rollout score jitter range from 0..4 to 0..8

asi.hypothesis: More stochasticity in heuristic rollout tie/near-tie scoring might broaden exploration and avoid brittle deterministic choices.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score nearly returned to baseline (81), with h2h and 4p heuristic much worse and more timeouts.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not increase jitter above 0..4; excessive rollout noise overwhelms heuristic signal.

description: Decrease heuristic rollout score jitter range from 0..4 to 0..2

asi.hypothesis: Slightly less rollout stochasticity might keep useful diversity while reducing noisy move choices.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell below baseline to 75, with many more timeouts and poor 4-player win counts.
asi.next_action_hint: The original 0..4 jitter magnitude is a local optimum for this workload; avoid further jitter magnitude tuning unless changing tie-breaking architecture.

description: Add root eval bonus for each eliminated opponent

asi.hypothesis: Average-opponent evaluation may fail to reward progress from eliminating non-root players in multiplayer games; a bonus per eliminated opponent might encourage closing games.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 87 across all workloads; the bonus appears to distort nonterminal values or encourage bad aggression.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add explicit eliminated-opponent bonus. Terminal reward and material/coup pressure are sufficient; focus on action policy/eval threat details.

description: Increase nonterminal eval sensitivity by changing denominator from 100 to 80

asi.hypothesis: A steeper material-to-reward mapping may make rollout evaluations distinguish good states more clearly.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 85; steeper eval hurt both 4-player workloads badly.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not make eval more extreme; if tuning scale, try a flatter denominator or non-linear terms with care.

description: Flatten nonterminal eval sensitivity by changing denominator from 100 to 120

asi.hypothesis: A flatter material-to-reward mapping may avoid overreacting to noisy intermediate states in imperfect information rollouts.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 90. 4p heuristic improved slightly, but 4p random collapsed and h2h dipped.
asi.next_action_hint: Denominator 100 is better aggregate; flatter eval is only promising if specifically optimizing 4p vs heuristic.

description: Double target coin weight in heuristic attack target scoring

asi.hypothesis: Attack actions should prioritize rich opponents more because high coins represent coup threats; target_score may underweight target coins.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 98. H2h improved and 4p heuristic nearly held, but 4p random lost enough to miss aggregate best and timeouts increased.
asi.next_action_hint: Higher target coin weighting is a possible h2h/heuristic idea but not aggregate-best; consider a smaller 1.5x integer approximation or threat threshold bonus.

description: Add target threat bonus when attack target has 7+ coins

asi.hypothesis: Targeting opponents who can coup soon should improve defensive attack selection without over-weighting every coin.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 99 to 80, wiping out all retained gains in the benchmark.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not add simple target coin-threshold bonuses in rollout scoring; they appear to distort target selection badly.

description: Select final ISMCTS move by total accumulated reward

asi.hypothesis: At low iteration counts, final mean reward can overfit sparsely visited lucky moves, while visit count alone lost value signal; total reward may better combine confidence and payoff.
asi.learning: New best strength_score=103. It improves all three workload components over current best: 4p_random 36, 4p_heuristic 21, h2h 46. Runtime/decisions rose moderately but primary strength improved.

description: Use parent node visits instead of edge availability in ISMCTS UCB exploration term

asi.hypothesis: Standard UCT uses parent visit count in the exploration logarithm; replacing ISMCTS availability count might improve low-iteration exploration.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 103 to 95, mostly from h2h dropping to even and 4p heuristic losing wins.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep availability-based exploration for ISMCTS; it better handles imperfect-information move availability than parent visits.

description: Compare eval root material against strongest living opponent instead of average opponent

asi.hypothesis: In multiplayer Coup, beating the strongest remaining opponent may matter more than average opponent material; max-opponent comparison could improve threat awareness.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 103 to 91, with 4p random especially poor.
asi.next_action_hint: Average opponent material remains better than strongest-opponent material; max threat focus likely over-defensive in multiplayer.

description: Model non-root players with random moves during ISMCTS tree simulation

asi.hypothesis: Because one benchmark component has random opponents, using random non-root moves in tree simulation may prevent overestimating heuristic opponent strength and improve exploitation.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell slightly from 103 to 102. It massively improved 4p_random (55 wins) but collapsed 4p_heuristic and h2h, so not aggregate-best.
asi.next_action_hint: Opponent model choice is highly workload-sensitive. Keep configured heuristic opponent model for aggregate; a future adaptive opponent model could switch based on observed opponent behavior.

description: Mix 25% random opponent moves into ISMCTS non-root simulation

asi.hypothesis: A mixed opponent model could capture both random and heuristic benchmark opponents better than all-heuristic or all-random non-root simulation.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary strength_score fell from 103 to 95; h2h suffered and timeouts rose. A fixed stochastic mix does not balance workloads well.
asi.next_action_hint: If pursuing opponent modeling, try explicit opponent inference rather than random mixing inside every simulation.

description: Raise balanced heuristic challenge base score from 12 to 18

asi.hypothesis: Balanced rollouts were too reluctant to challenge plausible but valuable claims because PassChallenge=25 beats many challenge scores; a modest base increase should better punish bluffs without making impossible-claim logic brittle.
asi.learning: New best strength_score=110. The gain is concentrated in 4p vs heuristic (21→28 wins) while 4p random improves slightly and h2h falls from 46 to 44. More timeouts, but primary improvement is large.
